accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE Year 1 Measurement programme of study ('measure and begin to record time (hours, minutes, seconds)') and its non-statutory guidance, NCETM Year 1 measures materials and the SI definition (1 minute = 60 seconds, 1 hour = 60 minutes). Everyday durations are typical, not exact: a blink lasts a fraction of a second to about a second, dentists (NHS) advise brushing for about 2 minutes, a night's sleep for this age is 10 to 13 hours. The frog's 3 seconds is a real 3-second wall-clock run measured with performance.now, and the sped-up sand in the last step is labelled '1 minute (sped up)' on the canvas and in the adult text.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-measurement slips: a minute is 100 seconds (step 2 prediction option 100, 'It is full. 60 seconds…not 100' message, m1, challenge tag hundred), choosing a unit that is far too short or long (step 1 'Too short!' and 'Too long!' messages, p1, p5, m3, m9, challenge long/short), stopping a stopwatch early or late (step 3 'Too soon' and 'Too late' replies, m4, challenge stopat), confusing a duration with a time of day (step 4 o'clock distractors, p4, m7, challenge oclock), and counting turns of a 1-minute timer (step 5 one or three turns, p2, m5, challenge once).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsecs is about measuring a duration with a unit: sorting jobs by seconds, minutes or hours, filling a 1-minute sand timer in 10-second scoops beside a 60-dot frame, a live stopwatch race against a hopping frog, writing a timing as a number plus unit, and turning a sand timer to brush for 2 minutes. flagdur compares two time bars started together, flaghr60 winds the clock hand for 60 minutes and 24 hours, flagtomin reads a clock to the minute; none uses a stopwatch, a sand timer or unit choice. Gate similarity is at most 9% to any lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds 60 by filling the timer until it will take no more sand, sees the stopwatch reading only matches the frog when Stop is pressed as it lands, finds that an o'clock answer is rejected as a time of day, and that one turn of the timer reaches only 1 minute while three turns overshoot. The task text then names the rule that was just seen.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then tests: 'Brushing your teeth takes about 2 … seconds' (the sort says too short), 'How many seconds make 1 minute? 10 or 100' (the timer fills at 6 scoops of 10), and 'To brush for 2 minutes, turn it 1 time' (Done after one turn says that was only 1 minute). A fourth asks whether 3 hops take seconds or minutes, which the live stopwatch settles.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions; wrong answers carry seven distinct messages: 100 seconds, only 10 seconds, a unit that is too long, a unit that is too short, o'clock for a duration, one turn for three, and stopping the stopwatch at a set number or before the job ends. Each names the slip and restates the rule in kid words.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 1.1 and adult at 6.9 (limits 5.5 and 10.5). Kid sentences are short with everyday jobs (blink, brushing teeth, a night of sleep); the adult text names the Year 1 statement, CCSS K.MD.A.1-2 and the key words duration, stopwatch, sand timer. Canvas labels are two or three words: 'a blink', '+10 seconds', 'Start', 'Done brushing'.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea: the three units, 60 seconds in a minute, using a stopwatch, recording with a unit. Items spread across unit choice (p1, p5, m3, m9), 60 seconds (p3, m1, m2, m8), the stopwatch (p4, m4, m6), timer turns (p2, m5) and o'clock (m7) with no repeated stems.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and desktop light and dark screenshots of every step at the start and after Show me. At 360 px the six job cards sit in a 3 by 2 grid with short labels above three full-width unit boxes, the 60-dot frame and its 10 to 60 labels fit beside the sand timer, the frog crosses the pond above a wide Start/Stop tile, the three record answers stack as full-width tiles, and the turn timer and Done tile fit; nothing is clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: the next job with seconds, minutes and hours buttons, Add 10 seconds, Start and Stop the stopwatch, each record answer, Turn the sand timer and Done brushing. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action and announces the stopwatch each second while it runs. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13.
